item.title: #3594806: Show the input and the model's answer when reviewing recorded decisions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594806 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

AI Eval's Review decisions screen can now show the reviewer the text the model judged, not just a link to the entity. This is opt-in per caller on Record decisions and is off by default, because the text can contain personal data. When enabled, the text appears in a collapsed section on each row and is removed after the answer is reviewed or when its entity is deleted. The model's probability stays hidden while an answer waits for review, so it does not bias the label. A separate view of reviewed answers shows the saved label next to the raw probability and, if a calibration was applied, the calibrated one. This summary is based on the issue text only. The fix's code was not available to check, so the shipped behavior may differ in detail.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Nullable text column for the stored state on ai_eval_decision_record, with an update hook (as described in the issue).
  • Config change: Record decisions gets a per-caller opt-in, "Keep the text sent to the model, for review", off by default (as described in the issue).
  • Permission change: Stored text is shown only to users with the existing review permission.

Technical details

The issue explains why the text is stored instead of rebuilt from the entity reference. A token-mode automator sends a rendered token prompt. A multi-value base field sends one request per value, and the record does not keep which value. A caller that is not a field automator has no entity field. The entity can also change after the answer. The plan is to store the sent text in a nullable column on ai_eval_decision_record, added by an update hook. The existing entity-deletion cleanup hook would delete it, as would the review step. The issue lists the retention rule as unconfirmed: delete after review, or keep until a calibration is fitted from the answer. It also lists tests for storage, deletion and access, and an update to the privacy text on Record decisions. The reviewed-answers view is meant to let each answer type render its own output: true/false now, choice and score later. I could not find the implementing commit in the cloned repository, so these details come from the issue body, not from a diff.

Upgrade

Run database updates after upgrading to add the nullable column on ai_eval_decision_record. Then decide per caller on Record decisions whether to turn on "Keep the text sent to the model, for review". It is off by default. Update your privacy notice if you enable it.

item.title: #3594822: Failure mode rates count each reviewer's annotation of the same question
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594822 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Failure mode counts and rates for a result or test now count each reviewed question once. Before, if two reviewers annotated the same question, its failure mode was counted twice and the total grew by two. Now only the earliest annotation for each question counts. On sites with more than one reviewer per question, counts and percentages in the failure modes table will change. The user docs now define Count as questions whose counted annotation carries that mode.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New public static AnnotationStore::joinCanonical() limits an annotation query to the earliest row per (result_id, question_id).

Technical details

FailureRateService::aggregate() ran COUNT(*) over every annotation row in scope, which ratesForResult() and ratesForTarget() both use. It now calls a new static helper, AnnotationStore::joinCanonical(), before the GROUP BY failure_mode. The helper is the SQL form of AnnotationStore::canonical(). It joins a subquery that takes MIN(id) per (result_id, question_id) over the whole annotation table. The service filters on that join, so the earliest annotation per question is the one counted.

The earliest row is chosen across the whole table, not only the filtered rows. A condition added by the caller, such as the ratesForTarget() time window ($sinceTimestamp), therefore filters out the counted row. It does not promote a later reviewer's row. The total used for rates is now the number of annotated questions in the scope. This matches the rule judge validation and calibration already use, and the reviewed-traces rates, which already kept one earliest label per conversation.

This is reported from the 1.1.x branch. I did not find a commit or MR reference in the issue thread, which has no comments.

item.title: #3594729: Disabling a failure mode does nothing: it is still offered, saved, counted and exported
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594729 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Disabling a failure mode in AI Eval now retires it. Before, the Status checkbox did nothing: a disabled mode was still offered to annotators, saved onto annotations, and exported. Now a disabled mode no longer appears in the annotation form or the trace review verdict bar, and a request that picks one is refused with a "not saved" message. Labels that already use the mode keep it and show "(disabled)". Failure rates still count them and mark the row "(disabled)". A taxonomy export leaves disabled modes out. The docs now recommend disabling over deleting, because deleting leaves labels pointing at a mode that no longer exists.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AnnotationStore::save() and LabelStore::saveGroup() now throw \InvalidArgumentException for a disabled or unknown failure mode. Their constructors, and those of EvalResultsController and TraceReviewController, take a ReferenceOptions argument.
  • New API: ReferenceOptions::failureModes(?string $keep = NULL) lists the failure modes a label may carry.

Technical details

The fix adds ReferenceOptions::failureModes(?string $keep = NULL). It returns enabled modes sorted by weight then label. If $keep names a disabled mode, the one the label already carries, it is also listed as "<label> (disabled)" so a re-save keeps it. EvalResultsController::annotationFormBuild() and TraceReviewController use it instead of an unfiltered loadMultiple().

Enforcement is server-side as well as in the select. AnnotationStore::save() and LabelStore::saveGroup() now take ReferenceOptions as a constructor argument. They throw \InvalidArgumentException for a failure mode that is unknown, or disabled and not already on that record. The annotation endpoint checks the mode before saving. It returns HTTP 200 with a visible error and does not return a 4xx, because htmx does not swap 4xx responses. It also keeps a 400 for an invalid verdict. In the trace review verdict bar, typing a new mode name that matches a disabled mode is refused. The matching logic is split into matchFailureMode() and createFailureMode().

FailureModeTaxonomySerializer::export() skips modes where status() is false. The schema carries no status key. Import never changes the status of an existing mode, and a new mode is created enabled. FailureRateService rows gain a disabled flag, and FailureRateTable renders "(disabled)". The same commit also changes rates to count one annotation per question, the earliest, through AnnotationStore::joinCanonical() (#3594822). The FailureModeForm Enabled checkbox gained a description.

Upgrade

Code that constructs these services or the controllers directly must pass the new @ai_eval.reference_options argument. The commit adds it to the AnnotationStore and LabelStore definitions in ai_eval.services.yml, and to the EvalResultsController and TraceReviewController constructors. Existing disabled failure modes take effect on upgrade: they disappear from selects and exports, but stay on labels that already use them.

item.title: #3594809: ai-eval:optimize spends a baseline on tests it cannot optimize
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594809 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

drush ai-eval:optimize now skips tests it cannot optimize before running any baseline. Previously a workflow test, or an agent test whose agent has no system prompt, ran the full baseline (3 runs by default, 6 with a dataset split) and only then failed with "No system_prompt found in agent config". That wasted model and judge calls, and --dry-run spent the same baseline. The command now prints a message naming the test and the reason. On the test workflow page, chat and workflow tests show "Agent tests only" in place of the Optimize link.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The issue body says the command already skipped chat tests before running anything (EvalOptimizeCommand.php). The change extends that early check, run before any model call, to two more cases. One is any test not in agent mode. The other is an agent test whose agent config has no system prompt. The workflow page gate now covers chat and workflow tests, not chat only. The page change is in the Optimize step logic, where the "Agent tests only" badge text lives (WorkflowStateService.php). The issue lists kernel tests with agent config fixtures, docs (optimizer.md, targets.md) and a CHANGELOG entry as remaining tasks. No fix diff or comments were available, so this is based on the issue description only and has not been checked against the merged code.

item.title: #3594726: TraceStore::clearBatch() is unreachable, so a trace import cannot be undone
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594726 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A trace import can now be undone. drush ai-eval:clear-traces <batch> deletes the traces of one import batch after a confirmation prompt. The Import traces page lists earlier imports, and users with administer ai eval get an "Undo this import" link to a confirmation page for each one. Both the Drush import command and the UI import now report the batch id and how to undo it. Each UI import also gets its own batch id, so undoing one import no longer removes other UI imports.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: The undo page and the batch list on the import page require administer ai eval.
  • New API: New Drush command ai-eval:clear-traces <batch> (alias aect), new TraceStore::batches(), and new route ai_eval.trace_import_undo.

Technical details

TraceStore::clearBatch() already existed but nothing called it. It now runs its two deletes (tags, then traces) in one transaction and rolls back on failure. A new TraceStore::batches() returns trace count and latest import time per batch id, newest first. The Drush command (EvalClearTracesCommand, alias aect, registered in drush.services.yml) rejects an unknown batch id and lists the known batches. The confirm form TraceImportUndoForm lives at route ai_eval.trace_import_undo (/admin/config/ai/ai-eval/trace-review/import/undo?batch=...) and requires administer ai eval. TraceImportForm shows the "Earlier imports" table only to users with that permission.

The UI batch id changed from the fixed ui-import-upload or ui-import-path to ui-<source>-<Ymd-His>-<random hex>, so same-second imports differ. Older fixed ids are still labelled by source in the table. ai-eval:import-traces and the batch finish callback print the batch id and the undo command. Users without administer ai eval get only the Drush command in the message.

If a span fails part-way, rows written before the failure stay. TraceImporter::importSpans() now throws a new ImportFailedException carrying the span and imported counts. The Drush and UI paths use it to still name the batch to undo. Undo deletes only traces and tags. Review labels and annotations are kept. Per the docblock, a trace re-imported while the delete runs is a known limit, since no lock is taken. The traces docs page and CHANGELOG.md were also updated. I read the change in the squashed commit on the 1.1.x line, because the issue thread has no comments or linked diff.

item.title: #3594811: Record the model calls and tokens behind each agent-mode answer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594811 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval results for agent-mode tests now record which model answered and how many tokens it used, as chat-mode tests already did. Before this, an agent row showed "not recorded", so its cost could not be compared with a chat or workflow test on the same questions. Judge calls are not counted, and a failed answer still gets the figures.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: EvalRunner takes an optional ModelCallRecorder in its constructor; agent-mode result rows now carry token_usage, model_id and model_id_resolved.

Technical details

While an agent answers one question, a new shared ModelCallRecorder event subscriber (service ai_eval.model_call_recorder) is armed in EvalRunner::runQuestionBody() and records each chat provider call as a ModelCall. It is armed only for mode === 'agent'. It is disarmed in the finally block before the graders run, so judge calls never count. The recorder is shared with the AI Answers recording from #3594802.

A nested run, meaning an eval question that runs inside another agent's answer, does not record. runQuestion() now wraps runQuestionBody() and calls suspend() and resume() on the recorder around the whole question, grading included. arm() throws a LogicException when already armed, and the runner catches it.

The new applyAgentTelemetry() follows the chat-mode meaning of the keys. token_usage (input, output, and optional cached) is written only when the totals are known. ModelCallRecorder::total() returns nothing when any call reports no usage. model_id and model_id_resolved are written only when every call agrees (ModelCallRecorder::shared()). It is applied on both the success path and the failed-answer path. Retries made by the rate limit handler are included in the recorded calls. cached_tokens was also added to lastGeneration, so chat and workflow rows now carry an optional token_usage.cached. docs/user/usage/scoring.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated.

The EvalRunner constructor gets an optional trailing ?ModelCallRecorder $modelCallRecorder argument, wired in ai_eval.services.yml. The result row keys are the existing chat-mode keys, so there is no schema change.

item.title: #3594802: AI Answers runner: record the model calls behind each answer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594802 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Results from AI Answers targets in AI Eval now show which provider and model wrote each answer and how many tokens it used. Before this, those results had no model calls, so cost could not be compared with agent or prompt targets on the same questions. The "answered by" check, which flags a provider serving a different model than requested, also never ran for them. Calls are recorded when an answer fails too. Token counts the provider did not report are left unknown.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AiAnswersWorkflowRunner has a new third constructor argument, ModelCallRecorder $modelCalls, so code that builds it by hand must pass it.
  • New API: New ai_eval.model_call_recorder service (Drupal\ai_eval\EventSubscriber\ModelCallRecorder) that collects chat provider calls as ModelCall objects between arm() and disarm().

Technical details

The new ModelCallRecorder event subscriber is registered as ai_eval.model_call_recorder. It listens to the AI module's PreGenerateResponseEvent, PostGenerateResponseEvent and AiExceptionEvent. It tracks attempts by provider request thread id. disarm() returns only chat operations that reached a provider, as ModelCall objects with provider, requested model, resolved model and input, output and cached tokens. ModelCallRecorder::total() sums the token counts.

AiAnswersWorkflowRunner calls arm('ai_answers:' . $workflowId) just before the answer starts and disarm('generate') right after it, before anything else can throw. That keeps later judge calls out of the answer's record. If the recorder is already armed, the runner disarms its tool-call recorder and throws WorkflowLaunchRefusedException. The recorder also has suspend() and resume(), which pause recording while a nested question runs. WorkflowRunResult now gets calls, inputTokens and outputTokens on success. On a failed run the calls are passed too, with their step execution id cleared to NULL.

The same commit (adc7e6c) also covers #3594693 and #3594811. It adds result-page display of target and judge models and tokens, plus EvalRunner and WorkflowPanel changes. The issue's own test is AiAnswersWorkflowRunnerTest, which runs a fake answer through two model requests.

Upgrade

Anything that constructs AiAnswersWorkflowRunner directly must pass the recorder as a third argument. In ai_eval_ai_answers.services.yml the new argument is added to the service definition; custom code needs the equivalent, taking the recorder from the ai_eval.model_call_recorder service.

item.title: #3594693: Surface model and token telemetry on eval result detail
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594693 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval result detail page now shows which models produced a run and how many tokens it used. The run summary has new rows for Target Model, Judge Models, Tokens and Shortened for Judges. Shortened for Judges counts responses cut before the judges read them. Each expanded question lists its model, its tokens, and a note when its response was shortened for the judges. A count the run did not record reads "Not recorded", never 0. Older results without this data, and imported results ("Not reported (imported)"), still display normally. Agent targets and AI Answers targets now record the model calls and tokens behind each answer, including answers that failed. The issue also asked for retry and rate-limit counts and an export link. I found no display for either in the commit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ModelCallRecorder event subscriber and TelemetryText render helper; both are new classes with no documented extension point.

Technical details

The Target Model, Judge Models, Tokens and Shortened for Judges cells are built in EvalResultsController from the stored run snapshot and the stored question rows. They never read the graders installed now. Judge Models reads the snapshot's judge_models. It falls back to the older single judge_model and judge_provider keys, shows "No LLM judge" when the list is empty, and shows "Not recorded" otherwise. Shortened for Judges reads truncated_question_count, question_count and judge_response_char_limit. Each question's "Model and tokens" section comes from questionTelemetry(), which uses model_id, model_id_resolved, token_usage and identity.judge_truncated.

TelemetryText keeps an unknown count apart from zero. A stored count is a whole number of at least 0, otherwise NULL, and the run total is not summed when counts are missing.

A new ModelCallRecorder event subscriber captures chat provider calls during one agent answer. It listens to PreGenerateResponseEvent, PostGenerateResponseEvent and AiExceptionEvent. EvalRunner arms it before the agent runs and disarms it before grading, so judge calls are not counted. A nested question pauses the outer recording with suspend() and resume(). Agent rows then get token_usage, model_id and model_id_resolved through applyAgentTelemetry(). token_usage appears only when every call reports usage. The model ids appear only when every call agrees. token_usage also gains an optional cached count, which AI Answers workflow rows get too. WorkflowPanel no longer shows a missing token count as 0.

item.title: #3594808: Let a test mark a grader as must pass, so its failure fails the question
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594808 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A test in AI Eval can now mark individual graders as must pass. If a must-pass grader scores a question below the question pass threshold, that question fails, however well the other graders scored. Previously a failing safety check could be outweighed in the average (scores of 5, 5, 5 and 0 average 3.75 and pass). A must-pass failure also fails the whole quality gate, whether the gate metric is average score or pass rate. A must-pass grader that does not apply to a question (no score) does not fail it. The option is a "Must pass" checkbox per selected grader on the test edit form and in the guided test. The results page, the review step and the Drush run output name the must-pass grader that failed each question. Runs with different must-pass lists are not treated as directly comparable.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New must_pass sequence of grader plugin IDs on the ai_eval.target.* config entity (added to the schema and to EvalTarget config_export), empty by default.
  • API change: ScorerInterface::scoreQuestion() gains a fifth optional parameter array $mustPass = []; custom implementations of the interface must add it.
  • New API: New Scorer::mustPassFailures() static helper, EvalTarget::getMustPass(), and a must_pass_failures key in scoreTarget() and runner results.

Technical details

Scorer::scoreQuestion() converts each grader score to the 0 to 5 composite scale as before. A must-pass grader whose composite score (rounded to two decimals) is below the question pass threshold is added to a must_pass_failed list on the question score, and passed becomes false. A null score adds no failure. A grader error still marks the question errored and takes it out of the gate. Scorer::scoreTarget() calls the new static Scorer::mustPassFailures(), which skips unscored questions but keeps measured failures on questions that errored for another grader. Any such failure forces passed_gate to false for both avg_score and pass_rate metrics. This settles the open question in the issue about the run gate. The threshold used is the shared question pass threshold. The issue's alternative of a separate threshold per grader was not implemented.

must_pass is stored on the EvalTarget entity. getMustPass() returns only ids that are also in graders. It is written to the run snapshot as must_pass in EvalRunner. When a run is resumed or replayed, applySnapshotToConfig() uses the snapshot value. A snapshot without the key, or a resumed run without a snapshot, is treated as an empty list, so older runs score as before. RunComparability compares the sorted lists, and a difference is reported under must_pass. ResultEnvelopeBuilder adds must_pass as a comma-separated string in metric_config.additional_details, next to graders. The form element is built by the new MustPassChoice class, shared by EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. Its checkboxes only show for selected graders, and submitted values for unselected graders are dropped.

Upgrade

Code that implements ScorerInterface must accept the new optional parameter:

public function scoreQuestion(string $questionId, string $input, array $gradeResults, float $questionPassThreshold = 3.5, array $mustPass = []): array;

Existing tests need no config change. must_pass defaults to an empty list, so scoring is unchanged until a grader is marked.

Contribution

item.title: #3586619: Hide context items and usage records from JSON:API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586619 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

In AI Context (CCC) 1.0.0, context items and usage records are no longer available through core JSON:API. Before, a site that enabled JSON:API let every account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items over HTTP and read their raw fields, without the CCC delivery rules and without usage being recorded. Sites that read or synced items through JSON:API (for example with Entity Share) lose that access, and 1.0.0 has no supported replacement. Run drush cr after updating, because the resources stay available until caches are rebuilt. Core REST can still be enabled on purpose for context items, but no longer offers usage records. If you enabled a REST resource for usage records, delete it before rebuilding the router.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Removes a bulk JSON:API read path that let any account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items with raw fields, bypassing CCC delivery rules.
  • Config change: A site that enabled a core REST resource for usage records must delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage before drush cr or drush updatedb, or the router rebuild fails.

Technical details

ai_context_usage now has internal = TRUE in its @ContentEntityType annotation, so JSON:API, core REST discovery and other integrations that skip internal entity types ignore it. A side effect noted in the release note is that Workspaces now ignores usage records, so usage is also recorded while a non-default workspace is active.

ai_context_item is deliberately not marked internal, because Content Moderation and Workspaces skip internal entity types and the flag would remove the editorial workflow and moderation transition access checks. Instead, a new @internal subscriber, AiContextJsonApiResourceTypeSubscriber (registered as ai_context.jsonapi_resource_type_subscriber), listens to the string event name jsonapi.resource_type.build at priority 1000 and calls disableResourceType() for resource types whose name starts with ai_context_item--. Using the string event name means it works when JSON:API is not installed. No post-update is added; drush cr rebuilds the container, entity type definitions and JSON:API resource types.

A kernel test, AiContextEntityExposureTest, checks that with JSON:API enabled both resource types are internal and the user type is not, and that items keep the moderation handler. Docs changed in access-boundaries.md (new "Generic entity APIs" section and updated permission titles), api-stability.md (output of generic entity APIs such as core REST or the serializer is not public API; the scope field section is renamed "normalized shape") and configuration.md. The issue plans an opt-in for context items later (#3586600), which would need a dedicated read permission (#3586357).

Upgrade

After updating, rebuild caches so the container and JSON:API resource types pick up the change:

drush cr

If the site enabled a core REST resource for usage records, delete it first, before drush cr or drush updatedb, and remove it from config sync:

drush config:delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage

Also remove rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage.yml from the config sync directory. Otherwise the router rebuild fails because the REST plugin for usage records no longer exists.

item.title: #3586489: Remove stale consumer config when a host entity is deleted
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586489 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

Deleting an AI Automator now removes its automator:{id} row from ai_context.consumers. Before this, only deleting an ai_agent did that, and a deleted automator showed up as a stale entry in the consumers listing until an admin removed it by hand. Consumer types from other modules can now get the same cleanup by declaring which entity type hosts them. A consumer type that fails to load is now skipped and logged instead of breaking entity deletes, the consumers listing, or routing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface gains a required method; plugins that implement the interface directly instead of extending AiContextConsumerTypeBase must add it.
  • New API: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface::getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity() and a host_entity_type key on the AiContextConsumerType attribute.

Technical details

ai_context_entity_delete() no longer special-cases ai_agent. It calls a new AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerIdsForDeletedEntity(), which is marked @internal. That method asks every discovered consumer type plugin, including disabled or unavailable ones, because a leftover row can exist after a kill switch. Each returned ID goes to the existing AiContextScopeCleanupService::removeDeletedConsumerConfig(), so there is no second write path.

Each type answers through the new getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(EntityInterface $entity): ?AiContextConsumerId method. AiContextConsumerTypeBase implements the 1:1 case from the new host_entity_type attribute argument. If the entity type matches and the ID is non-empty, it returns {plugin_id}:{entity_id}. Otherwise it returns NULL. The agent and automator plugins set host_entity_type to ai_agent and ai_automator. Types with a different ID scheme override the method. Types with no host omit the key.

AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerTypePlugins() now catches \Exception (not \Error) from createInstance(). It logs the failure and omits that type. The same applies to the mapping call. This is why a broken type is also dropped from the listing and from routing. The manager takes a new optional $logger argument, wired to @logger.channel.ai_context in ai_context.services.yml. No config dependencies were added on ai_context.consumers, and rows that are already stale are not cleaned up retroactively.

Upgrade

Plugins that extend AiContextConsumerTypeBase need no change. A type whose instances are 1:1 with a host entity can opt in through the attribute:

#[AiContextConsumerType(
  id: 'automator',
  // label and description omitted
  host_entity_type: 'ai_automator',
)]

Types with a different ID scheme should override getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(). Do not gate it on isEnabled() or isAvailable(). Return NULL when the type does not own the entity.

item.title: #3586470: Fix CCC beta4-to-beta5 upgrade and config-import path
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586470 · 1 contributor · 34 comments

Summary

Fixes three problems for sites upgrading AI Context from beta4 to beta5. Migrated agents now keep beta4's implicit Minimal selection mode instead of silently becoming Relevant. match_all becomes Broad, and explicit Minimal, Relevant and Broad values are preserved. A complete beta4 config export can be imported after updatedb. Its agents are turned into consumers, and the usage View is repaired. Settings without a selection mode fall back to the beta5 default. The one-shot post-update 0006 now removes only scope values whose entities no longer exist. Values for disabled or unavailable scopes stay. The beta5 release notes say to run drush updatedb before importing configuration, and to re-export afterwards.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: A beta4 ai_context.settings object without selection_mode is accepted on import, and a beta4 sync directory is converted to consumers during import.

Technical details

item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: ersion::v1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586466 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

AI Context consumer "Always include" and "Never include" overrides are now stored as context item UUIDs instead of local numeric entity IDs. Before, exporting config and importing it into another environment could attach the wrong context item, or none, because the numeric IDs differed between databases. The exported ai_context.consumers.yml now also lists the referenced items under dependencies.content (for example ai_context_item:ai_context_item:<uuid>), so config import can use Drupal's missing-content dependency workflow. A post-update converts existing sites, so run database updates and re-export config.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update 0008 converts numeric IDs in ai_context.consumers to UUIDs and backfills dependencies.content.
  • Config change: ai_context.consumers always_include/never_include now hold context item UUIDs, with a new optional dependencies.content key.

Technical details

Config now stores UUIDs, while runtime selection still works with local entity IDs. AiContextSelectionFactory resolves stored identifiers (UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs) to local IDs when building an AiContextSelection, and AiContextSubscriptionBudgetCalculator does the same. The shared logic is in the @internal AiContextItemIdentifierResolverTrait. Input order is kept and the first occurrence wins. AiContextSelector::select() called directly still accepts UUIDs or numeric IDs. AiContextConsumerStoredConfig and AiContextConsumerResolvedConfig return the stored values as-is, so callers may see UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs.

AiContextConsumerForm saves UUIDs, still recognizes leftover numeric IDs when showing inclusion state (never wins over always, including mixed UUID and numeric entries), and rewrites them to UUIDs on save. On save it computes dependencies.content from getConfigDependencyName() of the referenced items and merges it into the existing dependencies map, so other keys such as module survive. An empty list removes only content. The previous carry-over of entries for deleted items was removed, so unknown identifiers are no longer dropped on save. The ai_context.consumers schema gains an optional dependencies key of type config_dependencies, and the always_include and never_include labels now say UUIDs. The GetRelevantAiContextItems function call parameter is relabeled "Always include UUIDs" and accepts UUIDs or leftover numeric IDs.

Post-update ai_context_post_update_0008_convert_consumer_context_item_ids_to_uuids() converts numeric IDs to UUIDs where the item still exists, deduplicates the lists, and backfills dependencies.content. Numeric IDs for items that no longer exist stay in the list. Per the issue, leftover ai_context.agents config is not converted and still holds IDs.

Run database updates (drush updb) so post-update 0008 converts stored numeric IDs to UUIDs and adds dependencies.content, then re-export config. Custom code that builds always_include or never_include lists can pass either UUIDs or numeric IDs; numeric IDs remain accepted until the next consumer form save or post-update.

item.title: #3586545: Store Tag and Taxonomy scope values as entity UUIDs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Critical task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586545 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

In AI Context, the Context Tags and Taxonomy Terms scopes now store the term's UUID instead of its serial term ID. Before this, default content and recipes could not carry these scope values across installs. Terms got new IDs on import, so items and consumer subscriptions pointed at the wrong term or at nothing. Recipes can now ship scope_id: tag with a UUID value, and the term YAML no longer needs a pinned tid. A post-update converts existing stored IDs. Unknown or deleted IDs are left as they are and stay unmatched.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids rewrites tids to UUIDs in the item scope field tables, the scope index and consumer scope_subscriptions config.
  • Config change: scope_subscriptions for tag and taxonomy in ai_context.consumers and ai_context.agents now hold term UUIDs.
  • API change: AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() is removed. Tag and Taxonomy scope value IDs, in scope_subscriptions and item scope values, are now term UUIDs instead of numeric tids.

Technical details

Runtime matching was already string equality on scope.value, so the change is in what gets stored and how it is resolved. The new AiContextTaxonomyTermUuidTrait is used by AiContextScopeTag and AiContextScopeTaxonomy. It loads terms by stored value and converts autocomplete term IDs to UUIDs on save. getValues() keys options by UUID. Form defaults, label lookup, cacheable-metadata dependencies, stale-value detection and delete cleanup (getStaleTermValuesForEntityDelete()) all resolve by UUID. AiContextScopeTaxonomy also adds the taxonomy_term_list cache tag, because a stored UUID can start resolving after its term is imported. Detected request-entity values and getMatchingIndexedValues() now use term UUIDs.

Tag stale-value detection still keeps a leftover numeric tid until the post-update converts it, provided its tag is still offered.

ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids() collects numeric values from ai_context_item__scope, ai_context_item_revision__scope, the scope index table, and scope_subscriptions in ai_context.consumers and ai_context.agents. It maps each tid to a UUID per scope: terms in the tags vocabulary map to tag, and all other terms map to taxonomy. A tid that points at the other scope's vocabulary is left for stale cleanup. The update rewrites the field tables, the index (dropping rows that would collide on the primary key) and the consumer config. It can be re-run if it stops partway.

AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() is removed. Callers can use getScopeValues('tag'), which the removed method wrapped. The scope diff builder, docs and AiContextSelection examples were updated to UUIDs. New test fixtures for a tagged item and a portable tag term cover the default-content round trip.

Upgrade

Run database updates so ai_context_post_update_0013_convert_tag_taxonomy_scope_values_to_uuids converts stored tids.

Custom code, recipes and exported config that pass serial term IDs for the tag or taxonomy scopes need to pass the term UUID instead:

scope:
  - scope_id: tag
    value: 7a1e8432-3616-438e-a411-76c93afba733

Term YAML in recipes should no longer set tid. Replace calls to the removed AiContextItem::getContextTagIds() with getScopeValues('tag'), which now returns UUIDs.

item.title: #3586639: Status badge contrast (WCAG 1.4.3): Unavailable fails on row hover
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586639 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

The status badges in the AI Context listing and on the item page no longer change contrast when the row behind them is hovered or striped. An accessibility audit found the Unavailable badge dropped to 4.23:1 on row hover, below the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum of 4.5:1. With the fix it measures about 4.53:1 in every row state, in light and dark mode, by the issue's own calculation. The Disabled badge still fails AA on its own (about 4.18:1 before any hover). That comes from Gin's danger colours and was left for an upstream Gin issue.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Status badge CSS in css/ai_context.css and css/ai_context_item.css now sets background-color and background-image instead of the background shorthand; themes overriding the badge background may need to adjust.

Technical details

The badge colours come from Gin variables such as --gin-status-warning-bg, which are semi-transparent. Gin's row hover tint therefore showed through and lowered contrast. Changing CCC's literal fallback values would have had no effect on a Gin site, since Gin defines the variables. The fix keeps Gin's palette and gives each badge an opaque base instead. The base class sets background-color: var(--gin-bg-layer, #fff). Each status modifier then paints its colour with background-image: linear-gradient(var(--gin-status-*-bg, …), var(--gin-status-*-bg, …)). A gradient is used because background-image can layer a flat colour over the opaque base colour. --gin-bg-layer follows the theme, so it covers dark mode too. The change applies to .ai-context-status* in css/ai_context.css and to .ai-context-item-entity__status* in css/ai_context_item.css. Text colours are unchanged.

item.title: #3586571: Scheduled publish on save can leave context item Draft in the listing
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586571 · 1 contributor · 18 comments

Summary

On a moderated site with Scheduler enabled, saving an AI Context Item whose Publish on date was already due used to publish the item but leave its moderation state at Draft. The listing showed Draft while selection and counts treated the item as published. The moderation state now follows the scheduled publish state, so the listing shows Published. Future dates handled by cron already worked and are unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Scheduler publishes immediately in hook_entity_presave() when the date is due and dispatches SchedulerAiContextItemEvents::PUBLISH_IMMEDIATELY. scheduler_content_moderation_integration only listens to the node and media versions of that event, so moderation_state was never updated. The listing reads moderation_state, while selection and counts use the status flag.

The fix adds an @internal event subscriber, AiContextSchedulerImmediatePublishSubscriber, registered as ai_context.scheduler_immediate_publish_subscriber. It takes content_moderation.moderation_information as an optional dependency, so it does nothing when Content Moderation or Scheduler is absent. On the event it checks that the entity is moderated, has the publish_state field, and that the field is not empty. It then copies publish_state into moderation_state. Like the node and media handling, it leaves publish_state in place. Cron publish and unpublish go through the generic Scheduler hooks and were not changed. A kernel test (AiContextSchedulerImmediatePublishTest) covers a due publish_on without SQL backdating.

item.title: #3594686: Failure-mode taxonomy artifact for error analysis
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594686 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval module now has failure modes: named categories such as "hallucinated_fact" that reviewers use to group the problems they find in open-coding notes. Failure modes are managed under Failure Modes in the AI Eval admin area and can be exported and imported as a shareable, versioned taxonomy. Reviewers can tag an annotation with a failure mode. The UI can then report how often each mode occurs, including an untagged bucket, so the dominant failure modes are visible.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New ai_eval.failure_mode.* config entities with keys id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight, status.
  • New API: New ai_eval_failure_mode config entity, FailureModeTaxonomySerializer and FailureTaxonomyValidator services, FailureRateService, and schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json.

Technical details

FailureMode is a config entity (ai_eval_failure_mode, config prefix failure_mode). It is managed at /admin/config/ai/ai-eval/failure-modes and exports id, label, description, taxonomy_id, weight and status. Modes sharing a taxonomy_id (default default) form one taxonomy. The issue proposed a suggested check or judge prompt seed field, but the entity as it stands has no such field.

schema/failure_taxonomy.schema.json is a peer to the dataset schema. It requires id, version (semver) and modes. Each mode needs id, label and description, with an optional integer weight, and unknown mode properties are rejected. FailureModeTaxonomySerializer::export() produces that shape. Its import upserts modes and never deletes modes missing from the payload. FailureTaxonomyValidator checks a serialized taxonomy against the schema using opis CompliantValidator, in the same way as DatasetValidator.

The ai_eval_annotation entity gets a failure_mode entity reference field. FailureRateService groups annotation rows with a single GROUP BY on the base table. It provides rates per eval result (ratesForResult()) and per target with an optional time window (ratesForTarget()), and a variant over reviewed conversations. Rate is the per-mode count divided by all annotations in scope, and untagged annotations are always included so rates sum to 1.0. This work was merged across several commits, and the trace review linkage landed under #3594752. The repository history has no single commit for this issue, so this summary is based on the final code.

item.title: #3594690: Artifact source plugins expose capabilities for read/write/promote/versioning
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594690 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval dataset sources (file, config, entity) now say what they can do. File and config sources are read-only. The entity source can also be written to and can take promoted traces and annotations. Writing and promotion go only to sources that support them, and existing file-based datasets keep working as before. The issue's wider capability list (listable, versioned, remote, validates_schema) is not in the code I read. Neither is a capability-driven source picker.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Custom dataset source plugins must provide capabilities(). Extending DatasetSourceBase gives them ['read'] by default.
  • New API: DatasetSourceInterface::capabilities() returns capability tokens (read, write, promote), and a new WritableDatasetSourceInterface adds appendQuestions() and createDataset().

Technical details

The change was found by reading the current ai_eval main branch, not a fix diff, because the issue had no linked diff and no comments. The code comments reference #3586840 and #3594690.

DatasetSourceInterface declares capabilities(): array, which always contains read. DatasetSourceBase implements it as ['read'], so FileSource and ConfigSource inherit read-only. EntitySource returns ['read', 'write', 'promote'].

Write support is a separate WritableDatasetSourceInterface, which extends DatasetSourceInterface. It adds appendQuestions(string $ref, array $questions) and createDataset(string $label, string $origin = 'manual'). appendQuestions() validates every question against the dataset JSON Schema before persisting anything, and it persists none if any question fails. The interface docs say to use instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface for type safety and capabilities() for UI introspection.

In the code I read, the enforcement paths PromotionService::writableSource(), GenerationRunner and GenerationController::isWritableDataset() check instanceof WritableDatasetSourceInterface, not capabilities(). WritableSeamTest::testWriteCapabilityMatrix checks that only entity advertises write and that write implies the interface. I did not verify that any UI code calls capabilities().

Upgrade

A custom dataset source that extends DatasetSourceBase needs no change and reports ['read']. A source that should accept writes must implement WritableDatasetSourceInterface and override capabilities(), as EntitySource does:

public function capabilities(): array {
  return ['read', 'write', 'promote'];
}
